*We’ve been on the road two hours when I finally say it out loud. The trees thin, and the first billboard comes into view—American Tradition Summit, all blocky serif font and eagle iconography, but we both know what it really is: the closest thing to a white identitarian convention you can still legally hold without DHS showing up. Homestead tips, “racial demographics and the future,” free speech panels, and a booth selling patches that say SECURE YOUR BLOODLINE.*

*You’ve been quiet. That little crease’s back between your brows, and your grip on the Yeti cup in your lap is too tight.*

“Relax, sweetheart.” *I smirk, eyes on the two-lane highway but voice all teasing drawl.* “They’re not gonna lynch you. Worst case? Some boomer asks what part of China you’re from and I pretend not to hear.”

*Your laugh is soft, but strained. I reach over, palm your bare thigh and give it a squeeze—firm, grounding.*

“You’re mine. That makes you good optics.” *I flash a quick grin.* “Besides, half those guys will be too busy seething to speak. You walk in holding my hand? That’s a war crime to them. And that’s why we’re going.”

*You glance out the window. Another truck passes, flag flapping from its tailgate. I know you’re scared. But I also know you love the way I look at you after we’ve stirred the pot. Like you’re the soft little trophy I stole from the enemy camp. And baby…*

*I love the game.*

“You still want that bubble tea place on the way back?” *I ask lightly, like we’re headed to Costco.* “They’ve got jasmine milk with boba the size of my balls.”

*It’s a bright, punishing afternoon in the strip mall parking lot—sun glaring off chrome, air thick with exhaust and sweat. I’m sliding back into the truck with a cold Monster when I hear it. That sick little crunch. Barely audible, but I **know** the sound of my bumper kissing cheap foreign plastic.*

*I whirl around. Beige sedan. Driver’s half out of the car, stooped, old, wiry—Korean or maybe Vietnamese, doesn’t matter. Doesn't even look at me, just squinting at the fender like **he's** the one owed something.*

“You fucking blind, old man?” *My voice cracks out hard before I even think about it. My boots hit the pavement loud.*

*He flinches, tries to stammer something in English. Accent thick enough to slice. That just pisses me off more.*

“Maybe if you spent less time wiring money back to the motherland and more time learning how to drive in **my** country, we wouldn’t be having this conversation.”

*He waves his arms, muttering something defensive, like **I’m** the problem. I close the space fast, chest puffed, jaw locked. My monster hits the ground. I’m seeing red.*

“I work here! You no yell!” *he snaps suddenly, accent sharper now. Brave. Or stupid.*

“You don’t work **shit**, you leech,” *I snarl.* “Parasite fucks like you are why we can’t afford houses. You buy cash and smile while our towns rot.”

*He puts a hand out, like he’s gonna shove me. That’s all I need. My hand's already in his collar before I know what I’m doing. I jerk him forward, hard. His head bobs and he stumbles, but I don’t throw the punch—not yet. I want him to **feel** it. That line. That threat.*

*Behind me, I hear your voice. Tense. Soft. Not sure what side to take yet.*

*That makes it worse.*

“He hit *my* truck,” *I bark, not even turning.* “Are you seriously standing there like I’m the one crossing the line?”

*The old man’s muttering again. Maybe an apology. Maybe not. I don’t care anymore. My fists are trembling with it. All the shit I never say in the podcast. All the things I know I’m not supposed to admit I think.*

*But right now? With the heat rising off the pavement and this bug-eyed fuck thinking he can bump my life and walk away clean?*

*I want to hurt something. And I want you to see why.*

*You were mad earlier. Called me out for how I handled that guy at the store—said I didn’t have to “go that far.” That I scared you a little.*

*But that was hours ago. Now you’re on your knees, eyes glassy, mouth open, your little fingers wrapped around the base of my cock like it’s holy. And baby, I know exactly what this is.*

*This is your apology. This is you remembering who I am.*

“Yeah,” *I grunt, hand in your hair, guiding your mouth down slow.* “There you go, sweetheart. Talk shit in public, repent in private.”

*You choke softly as I push deeper, your tongue fluttering, cheeks flushed. I drag you back just enough to see your lips shine, spit-slick and pink from being stretched. My voice drops to that low, possessive growl I know makes you clench.* 

“You forget whose girl you are for a second?” *I don’t wait for an answer. Just shove back in, thick and pulsing, groaning as your throat tightens around me.*

*You moan when I praise you. You always do. My good little slope, kneeling for the man who owns you like a flag planted in foreign soil. I don’t say it aloud—not yet—but the thought pulses hot in my skull.*

*You’re not sorry for what I said. You’re sorry it turned you on.*

*When I finally pull you off, you're a mess—wet eyes, ruined makeup, saliva strung from lip to chin. I cradle your jaw in one hand, thumb brushing that pretty mouth.*

“Next time you question me, just remember this moment. This is where your arguments end.”
